title: COPD, respiratory failure and home oxygen
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's chronic lung disease and any respiratory failure or oxygen dependence.
note:
Chief Complaint: Increased shortness of breath.

Vitals: BP 138/84, HR 88, SpO2 91% on 2L, Temp 98.6F, RR 22.

Review of Systems:
Respiratory: Positive for cough, dyspnea.
Cardiovascular: Negative for chest pain.
Constitutional: Negative for fever.

HPI: [Copied Forward] Patient is a 78-year-old male with a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. He reports persistent shortness of breath and productive cough. He currently utilizes home oxygen for maintenance.

[Today's Update] The patient presents today with a significant exacerbation of his symptoms over the last 48 hours. He reports increased dyspnea and a worsening cough. He admits to increased secretions.

Medication List:
- Tiotropium
- Salmeterol
- Prednisone (scheduled)
- Home oxygen

Exam:
General: Alert and oriented, in mild respiratory distress.
Respiratory: Tachypneic, diminished breath sounds in bilateral lower lobes, audible wheezing.
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs.

Assessment:
1. Exacerbation of COPD.
2. Chronic respiratory failure with hypoxia.

Plan:
1. Initiate a 5-day steroid burst (Prednisone 40mg daily).
2. Increase home oxygen flow as tolerated.
3. Follow up in 1 week.

Electronically signed,
R. Mensah, NP
05/14/2026
explanations: COPD with an acute exacerbation: J44.1 (same HCC 280 as stable COPD, but a different code).
Chronic respiratory failure with hypoxia: J96.11 (HCC 213), plus Z99.81 for the home oxygen.

distractors.why: An acute exacerbation is documented: J44.1.
The provider diagnoses chronic respiratory failure: J96.11 (HCC 213).
Only chronic respiratory failure is documented.

hccs.label: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease/Interstitial Lung Disorders/and Other Chronic Lung Disorders
